description: validateSpec validates criterion CONTENT (non-empty string plus no store-reaching recursive-search oracle) at filing time, and the same form becomes the named self-contaminating-search rule in the plan-time oracle lint.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirmed `--eval` / `-e` is a documented `bun run` flag ('Evaluate argument as a script. Alias: -e') and that inline eval input is treated as TypeScript-with-JSX, so every acceptance-criterion probe in this PRD (bun -e with an ESM import of a local .ts module) is a supported, non-deprecated invocation. No breaking change or deprecation affecting the probes; nothing else in this issue touches an external library API (the work is pure TypeScript string/regex validation).

userStories.title: Review round 2 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: CRITICAL [src/issues/self-contaminating-search.ts:293]: applyToken pushes the positional token VERBATIM as a search root with no stripping of trailing shell punctuation, so the canonical command-substitution form of a store-reaching search is not detected: `$(grep -rl zzqqx scripts)` tokenizes its root as `scripts)`, which isStoreReachingRoot (:178) rejects (normalized 'scripts)' is neither STORE_PATH nor an ancestor prefix). Measured end-to-end through BOTH real call sites: findStoreReachingSearch('test $(grep -rl zzqqx scripts) -gt 0') -> null, validateSpec(... [oracle: named-command test $(grep -rl zzqqx scripts) -gt 0]).ok === true, and lintPrd on the same criterion returns 0 self-contaminating-search findings. This is independent of the command-position work: `(grep -rl zzqqx scripts)` (open paren directly adjacent, so isCommandPosition is satisfied) is also null. The in-diff regression test that claims to cover exactly this shape (test/issues/self-contaminating-search.test.ts:119-122) passes only because it inserts an artificial space before the ')' -- no real command has that space -- and the real CAM-460 AC2 fixture only passes because a '| wc -l' pipe happens to end the clause before the ')'. Net effect: the primary defect class this PRD exists to refuse (US-002) and to flag retroactively (US-003) is not caught for the single most common shell idiom used to wrap it. Fix: strip trailing shell punctuation (')', unmatched closing quote, backtick) from a positional token before treating it as a root, or end the invocation's argument list at an unbalanced ')'. Add the space-free `$(grep -rl X scripts)` and `` `grep -rl X scripts` `` shapes as regression cases in both test/issues/self-contaminating-search.test.ts and test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts.

userStories.title: Review round 2 fix 002: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: CRITICAL [src/issues/self-contaminating-search.ts:207]: isCommandPosition's left-context allowlist (start-of-string, '|', '&', ';', '(', or the word 'xargs') does not accept an OPENING QUOTE, so a tool word appearing immediately after `-c '` or `-c "` is treated as non-invoked text. That is this project's dominant oracle idiom -- US-003's own AC3 oracle is literally `bash -c 'grep -q ... && grep -q ...'` -- so a store-reaching recursive search authored in the most natural wrapper evades both guardrails. Measured: findStoreReachingSearch(`bash -c 'grep -rl zzqqx scripts'`) -> null; (`bash -c "grep -rl zzqqx scripts"`) -> null; (`sh -c "rg -l zzqqx scripts/cam"`) -> null; (`bash -c 'test -n "$(grep -rl zzqqx scripts)"'`) -> null. End-to-end for each: validateSpec.ok === true and 0 self-contaminating-search lint findings. The same too-narrow enumeration also misses common command prefixes: `env FOO=1 grep -rl zzqqx scripts`, `sudo grep -rl zzqqx scripts`, and `xargs -0 grep -rl zzqqx scripts` / `xargs -n1 grep ...` (xargs is allowlisted but only when IMMEDIATELY adjacent to the tool word) all return null. Fix: accept a quote character and a backtick as command-position delimiters, and allow an intervening flag/assignment run before an allowlisted prefix word (xargs/env/sudo/time/command); add each measured shape as a regression case in both test files.

userStories.title: Review round 2 fix 003: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: WARNING [test/issues/self-contaminating-search.test.ts:120]: The test named 'still flags a genuine search hidden inside a $(...) command-substitution wrapper' is shaped to the implementation rather than to the behavior it claims to verify: it asserts on `'test $(grep -rl zzqqx scripts ) -gt 0'` with a space inserted before the ')'. Delete that one space (the form every real command actually has) and the test fails, because the root token becomes `scripts)`. The test therefore certifies coverage of the command-substitution wrapper class while that class is in fact undetected, which is precisely the tests-with-meaningful-assert failure mode: it is green for a reason unrelated to the behavior under test. Rewrite it to assert the space-free canonical form (and keep the spaced variant as a separate case if desired).

userStories.title: Review round 2 fix 004: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: WARNING [scripts/cam/patterns.md:1128]: The new durable patterns.md bullet records a capability claim that is measurably false, poisoning the canonical wisdom store for future stories. It asserts that re-tokenizing 'would make a genuine `$(grep -rl ... )` search hidden inside a `bash -c '...'` wrapper (CAM-460 AC2's own shape, and an existing regression test) invisible' and that 'isCommandPosition's char-adjacency check catches the `$(`-prefixed real invocation while still rejecting the four false-positive shapes above'. Measured on this HEAD: `bash -c 'grep -rl zzqqx scripts'` -> null and `bash -c 'test -n "$(grep -rl zzqqx scripts)"'` -> null, so the chosen design does NOT preserve wrapper-internal detection in general; it happens to work only for the exact spaced/piped fixtures in the test file. Per the project's own 'a comment does not prove behavior, verify the runtime' lesson, this bullet must be corrected in the same change that fixes the two CRITICALs, stating the actual boundary (which left-context delimiters are recognized and which are not) rather than an unqualified 'catches the real invocation'.

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: CRITICAL [src/issues/self-contaminating-search.ts:50]: SEARCH_TOOL_RE is matched against the RAW command text in findStoreReachingSearch (:243-249) before tokenization, so a tool-word match can BEGIN inside a quoted span or inside an unrelated hyphenated token. Combined with recursive:(tool==='rg') (:214) and roots.length===0 => root '.' (:253), any delimited two-letter 'rg' substring anywhere in the command produces a finding. Measured: findStoreReachingSearch('bun run gen-rg-report') -> {root:'.'}; ('grep -q "rg" scripts/cam/patterns.md') -> {root:'.'}; ('test -f docs/x.rg') -> {root:'.'}; ('bash -c "echo rg"') -> {root:'.'}. End-to-end this is a HARD REFUSAL on the issue-filing write path with no bypass: validateSpec returns ok=false for the legitimate criteria '... [oracle: named-command bun run gen-rg-report]' and '... [oracle: named-command grep -q "rg" scripts/cam/patterns.md]', with the misleading diagnostic 'recursive search root "." reaches scripts/cam/issues' for a command that performs no search at all. The second case directly contradicts the module's own documented safe form (:27-30, 'a single-file root under scripts stays legal even with -r') and the tests asserting it (test/issues/self-contaminating-search.test.ts:82-90), flipping only because the search NEEDLE is 'rg'; this is realistic because scripts/cam/patterns.md already contains 'rg ' as a delimited token twice and US-003's own AC3 oracle is exactly the shape grep -q "<needle>" scripts/cam/patterns.md. Fix: require the tool word to be in COMMAND position (start of string, or immediately after a clause separator / '(' / '$(' / 'xargs'), and derive tool candidates from the tokenized stream rather than a raw-text regex scan. Add the missing adversarial cases (tool word inside a quoted needle; tool word as a hyphen-delimited segment of an unrelated token) to test/issues/self-contaminating-search.test.ts and test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts.

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 002: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: WARNING [src/issues/self-contaminating-search.ts:189]: Two false-negative gaps let a genuinely store-reaching search past the guardrail. (1) applyToken only special-cases token === '--recursive', so the documented long form of -R is missed: findStoreReachingSearch('grep --dereference-recursive zzqqx scripts') -> null, even though man grep defines '-R, --dereference-recursive: Read all files under each directory, recursively'. (2) isStoreReachingRoot (:121-129) normalizes only a leading './' and trailing slashes, so an absolute root reaching the store is missed: findStoreReachingSearch('grep -rl zzqqx /Users/me/repo/scripts') -> null. Both are one-file mechanical fixes (accept '--dereference-recursive' alongside '--recursive'; strip a cwd prefix or match the store suffix for absolute roots) plus their test cases, in the same module the CRITICAL touches.

userStories.title: Refuse a blank or non-string acceptance criterion at filing time
userStories.description: As the issue-filing guardrail, I need validateSpec to reject any acceptanceCriteria element that is not a non-empty string, so that a single empty criterion can no longer satisfy the ADR-0051 plannability gate that the guardrail exists to enforce.
acceptanceCriteria: validateSpec recusa um criterio que nao seja string nao-vazia (aceita [""] e [123] hoje), e continua aceitando um criterio real. Swept RED on main 2026-07-30: exit 1; controle positivo afirmando o comportamento de hoje sai 0, provando que a sonda nao e vazia. [oracle: named-command bun -e 'import { validateSpec } from "./src/issues/spec.ts"; const mk=(a)=>validateSpec({acceptanceCriteria:a,scope:"s",gotchas:[],domainTerms:[]}); process.exit(mk([""]).ok===false&&mk([123]).ok===false&&mk(["AC1 is a real criterion"]).ok===true?0:1)']
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint/quality spine passes. [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes:
Files: src/issues/spec.ts (validateSpec, :31), test/issues/spec.test.ts (300 lines today, extend it).
- isNonEmptyString ALREADY EXISTS at src/issues/spec.ts:60 (module-private, used by validateSpecSource). Reuse it per element; do not reimplement and do not export it unless a later story needs it across modules.
- Today validateSpec only checks Array.isArray(ac) && ac.length !== 0, so [""] and [123] both pass and are persisted verbatim by buildIssueEntry (src/issues/alloc.ts:161), after which isPlannable's hasAcceptanceCriteria (src/issues/plannable.ts:35) measures only length. Element-level content validation is the single repair site for both symptoms.
- Keep the ValidationResult contract: one human-readable string per error pushed onto errors[], ok === errors.length === 0. Existing callers print each error (validateSpecGuardrail in src/commands/issue-file.ts:219 via printError; issue-specify.ts returns reason 'invalid-spec' with errors).
- validateSpec has TWO callers: the filing guardrail (src/commands/issue-file.ts:219, itself only reached when specSource !== undefined, i.e. --fast-track / --derived-from) and the spec interview (src/commands/issue-specify.ts:332). One rule here covers both ends; plain `cam issue --file-local` filing (stage:idea, no spec) deliberately never reaches the guardrail, so do not widen that gate.
- Do NOT export or re-export validateSpecGuardrail (issue-file.ts:219): it adds no rule of its own and the only runtime export of issue-file.ts is createLocalIssueOnMain.
- Regression risk to check before committing: existing fixtures in test/issue-file.test.ts and test/integration/issue-file-spec-channel.test.ts (e.g. acceptanceCriteria: ['The child issue behaves correctly']) must keep passing; only blank/non-string elements may start failing.
- Per patterns.md Oracle-falsifiability rule (scripts/cam/patterns.md:928), re-sweep the criterion probe RED on unmodified main before trusting it; it was verified exit 1 on main at plan time (2026-07-30).
- Probe-authoring trap (lived while writing the issue): a literal ']' inside a probe string closes the [oracle: ...] mark early (extractLastOracleRaw walks bracket depth), which yields a truncated command and a bash exit 2 that READS like a red sweep. The probes build brackets via String.fromCharCode(91/93) for this reason. If you edit any oracle text, re-drive parseOracleDirective (src/supervisor/behavioral-gate.ts:227) and diff the extracted command against the intended one; treat exit 2 or a stderr 'syntax error' as an extraction failure, never as red.

acceptanceCriteria: validateSpec recusa um criterio cujo oraculo e busca recursiva com raiz que alcanca scripts/cam/issues (raizes scripts, ponto, scripts/cam, e sem path nenhum), e ACEITA as quatro formas legitimas: leitura pontual via git show, busca com --exclude-dir=issues, raiz docs/adr, e raiz que e arquivo unico sob scripts. Swept RED on main 2026-07-30: exit 1 com extracao fiel confirmada via parseOracleDirective. userStories.notes:
Depends on US-001 (same function, same test file). Files: ONE new leaf detector module (recommended src/issues/self-contaminating-search.ts), src/issues/spec.ts, plus tests (new test/issues/self-contaminating-search.test.ts and/or extend test/issues/spec.test.ts).
- SHARED DETECTOR IS LOAD-BEARING: US-003 wires the plan-time lint rule to this SAME exported predicate. Two parallel implementations would drift and let filing accept what plan time blocks (or the reverse), so export one predicate (e.g. findStoreReachingSearch(command): { root: string } | null) from a leaf module both sides import. src/supervisor/behavioral-gate.ts has zero imports of its own, so importing parseOracleDirective from src/issues/* creates no cycle; verify with `bun run typecheck`.
- Extract the criterion's oracle command with the project's own parser (parseOracleDirective, src/supervisor/behavioral-gate.ts:227), never a hand-rolled regex; scan only named-command / file-assert directives, exactly like lintStoryCriteria (src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts:656).
- Recommended detection core, purely lexical and I/O-free (validateSpec must stay pure): a search invocation is recursive when it is grep/egrep/fgrep carrying -r/-R (bundled or separate) or rg (recursive by default); a root is STORE-REACHING when it is '.' , or a directory-ancestor-or-self of scripts/cam/issues ('scripts', 'scripts/cam', 'scripts/cam/issues', with or without a trailing slash), or when the invocation carries NO positional path at all (search defaults to cwd). The ancestor test makes the file-vs-directory distinction fall out for free: 'scripts/cam/patterns.md' is not an ancestor of the store, so a single-file root under scripts stays legal even with -r, and 'docs/adr/' is legal.
- Do NOT refuse a criterion merely for having no oracle, and do not require an oracle: many legitimate filings carry prose-only criteria, and requiring oracles here is a different (out-of-scope) gate. Only the contaminated FORM is refused.
- Blessed idiom that must stay ACCEPTED: pinpoint store read, `file-assert git show main:scripts/cam/issues/CAM-XXXX.json`, prescribed by .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md:102. It names a path, it does not descend.
- Explicit store exclusion must stay ACCEPTED: `--exclude-dir=issues` (and equivalent pathspec/glob exclusions) is exactly the shape of the intended repair for CAM-460 AC2, so refusing it would break the very fix this rule is meant to enable.
- Terminology: the new class is 'self-contaminating oracle'. patterns.md already uses 'self-nullifying' 5 times for a DIFFERENT defect (a zero-match scan passing in silence). Do not conflate the two terms.
- Sweep the criterion probe RED on unmodified main first (verified exit 1 at plan time, 2026-07-30) and re-drive parseOracleDirective on the probe text after any edit; a literal ']' truncates the mark and the resulting bash exit 2 reads as a false red (see US-001 notes).

userStories.title: Flag the same form at plan time as self-contaminating-search and record the class in patterns.md
userStories.description: As the plan-time oracle lint, I need a named self-contaminating-search rule reusing the filing-time detector plus the class written down in patterns.md, so that oracles already filed before the guardrail existed (CAM-460 AC2 today) are caught before a worker satisfies them with zero work.
acceptanceCriteria: O lint de plan time marca a mesma forma sob a regra nomeada self-contaminating-search e deixa a leitura pontual da loja limpa dessa regra. Swept RED on main 2026-07-30: exit 1; lintPrd devolve lista vazia hoje para a forma contaminada. [oracle: named-command bun -e 'import { lintPrd } from "./src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts"; const OB=String.fromCharCode(91),CB=String.fromCharCode(93);const M=OB+"oracle: ";const run=(c)=>lintPrd({userStories:[{id:"US-001",title:"t",acceptanceCriteria:[c]}]}); const bad=run("AC "+M+"named-command grep -rl zzqqx scripts"+CB); const ok=run("AC "+M+"file-assert git show main:scripts/cam/issues/CAM-0460.json"+CB); process.exit(bad.some(f=>f.ruleName==="self-contaminating-search")&&ok.every(f=>f.ruleName!=="self-contaminating-search")?0:1)']

A regra pega retroativamente o AC2 do CAM-460 como ele esta filado hoje, lendo o arquivo real da loja de forma pontual. Swept RED on main 2026-07-30: exit 1; a sonda le 6 criterios reais e os achados de hoje sao dois frozen-comparand, por isso a assercao exige o ruleName novo e nao findings.length, que ja seria verde. [oracle: named-command bun -e 'import { lintPrd } from "./src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts"; import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"; const acs=JSON.parse(readFileSync("scripts/cam/issues/CAM-0460.json","utf8")).spec.acceptanceCriteria; const f=acs.flatMap(c=>lintPrd({userStories:[{id:"US-001",title:"t",acceptanceCriteria:[c]}]})); process.exit(f.some(x=>x.ruleName==="self-contaminating-search")?0:1)']

patterns.md registra a distincao com o termo novo self-contaminating oracle e cita a exclusao explicita da loja como forma segura. Swept RED on main 2026-07-30: exit 1, ambas as ancoras com count 0; controle positivo com ancora existente (Oracle-falsifiability rule) sai 0. [oracle: named-command bash -c 'grep -q "self-contaminating oracle" scripts/cam/patterns.md && grep -q "exclude-dir" scripts/cam/patterns.md']
A espinha de qualidade passa. Este criterio e gate de nao-regressao, nao detector de mudanca: e verde na main hoje por construcao e nao foi varrido vermelho. [oracle: named-command bun run check:all]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]

The module header advertises a 'Pure lexical scan, no I/O' contract (:15) but isStoreReachingRoot now reads process.cwd() at :185, making the predicate's result environment-dependent (a filing run whose cwd is not the repo root classifies the same absolute root differently, falling through to matchesStoreSuffix). The behavior is still correct because the suffix fallback covers the store-relevant cases, but the header claim should be amended, or the cwd made an optional injected parameter defaulting to process.cwd() so the dependency is explicit and testable without relying on the ambient cwd (test/issues/self-contaminating-search.test.ts:143-152 currently builds its fixtures from process.cwd()).

findSelfContaminatingSearchErrors emits an identical error string per offending criterion with no index or excerpt identifying WHICH criterion offended, so a spec with two contaminated oracles produces two byte-identical messages and the author cannot tell them apart. Include the criterion index (or a truncated excerpt) in the message, consistent with how the surrounding validators name the field they rejected.

`ac.every((c) => isNonEmptyString(c))` does not narrow, forcing the `ac as string[]` cast at :80. Making isNonEmptyString a type predicate (`v is string`) would let the every() call narrow ac to string[] and remove the cast, with no behavior change and one fewer unchecked assertion on the filing write path.
